clue.text: O Tamur! (if you, like its slayer, need a clue)

definitions.text: O Tamur! (if you, like its slayer, need a clue)

parts.words: O Tamur! (if you, like its slayer, need a clue)
parts.note: O TAMUR is six of the eight letters jumbled; the missing two must be supplied, and the beast's slayer Theseus needed a clue, the ball of thread, to escape its labyrinth

explanation.surface: An exclamation addressed to someone called Tamur, with a teasing aside about needing help.
explanation.walkthrough: O TAMUR rearranged is short of I and N, so the clue is incomplete on purpose: you need a hint, as Theseus did. A 'clue' (clew) was the ball of thread Ariadne gave him to find his way out of the Cretan labyrinth.
explanation.definitionFit: The bull-headed monster of Crete was killed by Theseus, who found his way out of the labyrinth with a thread.

clue.text: Mr Smee, one crazy duck !

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: crazy says the letters of Mr Smee and the one are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Captain Hook's bosun Mr Smee is declared a mad duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' is a verb here: to dip under water.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck someone is to plunge them under water, to submerge them.

clue.text: Pass mark

parts.note: read not as the score needed in an exam but as going past a target: to pass the mark you aimed at

explanation.definitionFit: To go beyond an intended target, such as a runway or a goal, is to fly or shoot too far.

clue.text: Omit letter — a turn-up for a Roman magistrate

indicators.note: in a down clue a turn-up sends the letters upward, so the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: to elide is to leave out a sound or letter in speech

explanation.surface: A grammatical note on dropping a letter, said to surprise a Roman official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a turn-up' reverses ELIDE + A (ELIDEA) to give the answer reading upward.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Rome this official supervised public buildings, games and markets.

clue.text: Prisoner's follower in Ruritania

parts.note: the Prisoner is The Prisoner of Zenda, Anthony Hope's novel set in Ruritania; its follower is the sequel, named after the villain

explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Hope's sequel to The Prisoner of Zenda, set in the same imaginary kingdom, takes its title from its dashing villain.

clue.text: Type of electricity; it's seen in cats in a roundabout way

indicators.note: going round in a circuitous way suggests the letters of it and cats are shuffled

parts.note: the possessive 's adds no letter, so it gives IT

explanation.surface: Stroking a cat's fur can produce sparks of electricity, as the clue playfully notes.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface truth that cats' fur crackles helps hide that IT and CATS are anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Charge that builds up on a surface rather than flowing as a current is called by this name.

clue.text: Sausages, the Spanish variety surrounded by cabbages

indicators.note: surrounded by puts the first piece inside the second, the cabbages enclosing the article

parts.note: savoys are a crinkly-leaved variety of cabbage
el is the Spanish for 'the'

explanation.surface: A recipe of Spanish sausages served wrapped in cabbage leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety' links the article to the cabbages, hinting that savoy is a variety of cabbage. A saveloy is a spicy British smoked pork sausage sold in fish-and-chip shops.
explanation.definitionFit: A seasoned smoked pork sausage, popular in British chip shops, is one of these.

clue.text: Working hard to get one fish

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
ling is a long cod-like sea fish

explanation.surface: Someone toils away in the hope of catching a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Labouring with great effort is a synonym of working hard.

clue.text: Possibly net ten fish without being satisfied

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the fish wraps round the other letters

parts.note: the cod is a common food fish

indicators.note: possibly signals that net ten could be rearranged into another order

explanation.surface: An angler is content even though he might land ten fish in the net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking; read as 'lacking', the clue seems to say something is missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Being content is being pleased and happy with what one has, a synonym of satisfied.

clue.text: Threaten to write Finis to a Lincoln figure

parts.note: the Lincoln Imp is a famous small stone carving in Lincoln Cathedral
finis is Latin for the end, written at the close of a book

explanation.surface: Writing the end to a story about Abraham Lincoln is a menacing prospect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lincoln' suggests the president, but it is the English cathedral city, whose carved Imp is its emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: To hang over as an imminent danger is to loom, menace or threaten.

clue.text: Show-place for a VIP eccentric celebrity

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters of a VIP are reordered

parts.note: a lion is a celebrity much sought after in society, a social lion

explanation.surface: An exhibition hall laid on for an oddball famous guest.
explanation.definitionFit: A large tent or building put up for an exhibition or show is a show-place.

clue.text: Jacob going the rounds at Peniel

definitions.text: Jacob going the rounds at Peniel

parts.words: Jacob going the rounds at Peniel
parts.note: in Genesis Jacob grapples all night with a stranger at Peniel; going the rounds is read as bouts of a fight

explanation.definitionFit: Jacob grappled with an angel at Peniel, making him a fighter who throws opponents in bouts.

clue.text: One Jew or six in the Paris season

indicators.note: in puts the six inside the French season, its letters set within

parts.note: l'été is French for the summer, the season as spoken in Paris
six is the Roman numeral VI

explanation.surface: A man wonders whether one Jew or six will spend the season in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Paris season' asks for a French word, here the summer with its article attached.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the tribe of Levi, who assisted the priests in the Temple, was a Jew.

clue.text: Evil spirit, eg rum ?

explanation.definitionFit: A fiend is an evil spirit, and alcohol has long been called 'the demon drink', so rum is an example.

clue.text: He issued-the three-word version

parts.note: split 'issued' into 'is sued' and the clue describes the person who is taken to court

explanation.definitionFit: The person sued or accused in court is the one who answers the charge.

clue.text: Publisher's claim to ape the Tories

parts.note: to ape is to imitate, to copy
the Right is the conservative wing of politics, the Tories in Britain

explanation.surface: A publisher alleges that a rival is imitating the Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A publisher asserts legal ownership of the right to reproduce a work.

clue.text: Act as solicitor, meaning one is French

parts.note: import is the meaning or significance of something
une is the French feminine word for one

explanation.surface: A lawyer explains what a French phrase means.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitor' suggests a lawyer, but here it is someone who pesters or begs.
explanation.definitionFit: To pester someone with persistent requests is to solicit them, in the begging sense.

clue.text: Impeded a backward boy ?

explanation.definitionFit: Being obstructed is being impeded, and the word can also be read as hind-ered, kept behind like a backward child.

clue.text: Half-moon

parts.note: read not as a crescent shape but as half of a lunar month, a period of time

explanation.definitionFit: A moon in the sense of a lunar month is about four weeks, so half of one is a period of two weeks.

clue.text: Mother of twins, one hairy, one smooth

definitions.text: Mother of twins, one hairy, one smooth

parts.words: Mother of twins, one hairy, one smooth
parts.note: in Genesis Esau was a hairy man and his twin Jacob a smooth man; the clue asks for their mother

explanation.definitionFit: Isaac's wife bore the twins Esau and Jacob in the Book of Genesis.

clue.text: The rate's said to be reduced by hasty action

definitions.text: said to be reduced by hasty action

explanation.definitionFit: Velocity is a rate of motion, and the proverb 'more haste, less velocity' runs with this word.

clue.text: Put up journalist taking in Crete perhaps

indicators.note: taking in has the journalist enclosing the other letters, a container

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the crossword's stock journalist

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters of Crete may appear in another order

explanation.surface: A reporter is sent to cover the island of Crete.
explanation.walkthrough: Crete looks like the island the reporter visits, but only its letters are wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise or build something is to put it up.

clue.text: Securities that secured old offenders

explanation.definitionFit: Shares in companies are financial holdings, and the wooden frame that locked offenders' ankles for public punishment had the same name.

clue.text: Arrested Liszt for instance in North Dakota ?

indicators.note: in puts the cleric inside the state's abbreviation

parts.note: ND is the postal abbreviation for North Dakota
Franz Liszt took minor orders and was known as the Abbé Liszt; an abbé is a French cleric

explanation.surface: The composer Liszt is taken into custody in the American Midwest.
explanation.walkthrough: Liszt is not a composer here but an example of an abbé, the title he took late in life.
explanation.definitionFit: To be caught and taken into custody is to be nicked, collared or arrested.

clue.text: Not a sign of public officials

parts.note: Aries, the Ram, is the first sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A statement that certain public officials show no sign of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Officials authorised to witness and certify documents are public officers.

clue.text: Spanish pelican's one-time island prison

explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish word for a pelican named the island in San Francisco Bay that held a federal penitentiary until 1963.

clue.text: Many, out of practice, get irritable

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a large number
rusty means one's skill has faded from disuse

explanation.surface: Lots of people who have not practised get bad-tempered.
explanation.definitionFit: A gruff, short-tempered manner is described as crabby or irritable.

clue.text: Ran to earth red cat gone astray

indicators.note: gone astray means wandered off course, so the letters of red cat are scattered

explanation.surface: A lost ginger cat is finally tracked down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ran to earth' is hunting language: found after a chase.
explanation.definitionFit: To run a fox to earth is to chase it to its burrow, to locate or find it.

clue.text: Rocky — a French boyfriend ?

parts.note: un is the French for a or one
a steady is a regular boyfriend or girlfriend

explanation.surface: A woman asks if Rocky is a French boyfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocky' looks like a name, but it is the adjective: wobbly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rocky wobbles and is not firm, a synonym of shaky.
